title: Comparative-query retrieval coverage
hypothesis: A union metadata filter avoids dropping one named technology, while balanced multi-technology ordering increases two-sided coverage within topK=4 without reducing canonical evidence coverage.

variants.description: Reproduce the former behavior by retaining only the first technology recognized according to the historical detector order.
Search the union of both language partitions and keep the globally highest cosine scores.
Search the same union, assign a rank within each language, then order by language rank and cosine score as in the production pgvector query.

changedVariable: Comparative-query metadata filtering and top-k balancing policy
metrics: macro reciprocal rank across evidence sides
embedding cache hits, provider inputs, requests, and estimated cost

decisionRule.eligibility: A candidate must detect exactly both expected technologies for all eight cases and must not reduce mean canonical evidence-side recall or macro evidence-side MRR relative to legacy-first-technology.
decisionRule.primary: Choose the eligible candidate with the highest both-evidence-side coverage@4.
tieBreakers: prefer multi-technology-unbalanced over balanced when every quality metric ties because it is simpler
decisionRule.scope: This focused benchmark tests comparative answerable queries only; it does not recalibrate the 0.68 abstention threshold or estimate unanswerable false positives.
